articles.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
articles.excerpt: We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub's repositories to Azure. Here's how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently. The post The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Over the past year, while Git traffic grew exponentially, 99.99999% of the Git repositories on GitHub began living in two places at once: our own data centers and Azure. The rest are among the busiest on the platform, and they're held back by just one thing: a 25ms round trip.
In an earlier blog post , we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation storage architecture:

In this post, we'll look at the immediate bridge between our old design and our new one. We'll talk about how a change to the way our quorum serializes writes gets the busiest repositories into Azure, and how that same step opens the door to replicas that keep no persistent state of their own.

The timing and shape of the move were driven by the agentic shift: rapidly growing traffic, a hard ceiling on the power capacity of our data centers and the surrounding geographical region, and physical supply chain constraints. At the beginning of our migration, the remaining capacity with all possible expansion gave us enough time to migrate safely, but not enough to do it slowly.

While we had prototyped new architectural approaches for scaling Git on cloud infrastructure, changing the storage architecture and the hosting platform at the same time, under that growth, carried too much risk. Given our scale and how critical the service is to the community, we needed to sequence the work carefully: move the data first, then evolve the architecture once it arrived.

articles.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
articles.excerpt: Almost 100,000 Commerce.com domains now give AI agents real shopping tools through WebMCP on Cloudflare. Here's how we turned it on across every store at once, while keeping each merchant in control.
details: AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online.

That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML - they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it.
Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products .
Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable.

Because WebMCP is still an experimental proposed browser standard in early preview, it’s currently available behind experimental Chrome flags ( chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing ), in Chrome Origin Trials, in some agentic browsers, and across developer environments like Cloudflare Kitesurf .

articles.title: Uber brings ChatGPT Work to all employees with OpenAI
articles.excerpt: Uber is rolling out ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees, helping teams research, analyze data, create presentations, and complete complex workflows.
details: Uber announced the company-wide rollout of ChatGPT Work, an agent that helps employees take on a wide range of tasks within ChatGPT Enterprise, starting today.
The rollout will make ChatGPT Work available to more than 30,000 employees across Uber’s global workforce.
Expanding from an initial pilot of 1,000 employees, the rollout will give teams across Uber access to an agentic platform designed to take on complex, multi-step tasks and deliver finished work.
The expansion makes ChatGPT Work Uber’s first company-wide deployment of an agentic platform tailored for knowledge work.

ChatGPT Work connects with tools companies like Uber use on a daily basis, including Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, and Slack, enabling workers to research information, prepare meeting briefs, create presentations, analyze data and complete workflows across applications.

articles.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
articles.excerpt: Following the discovery that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates use weak keys, Cloudflare is deploying mitigations and releasing client updates. We explain the impact, our response, and what customers and developers should do next.
details: On October 19, 2026, at approximately 17:00 UTC, Cloudflare became aware that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised.
These certificates were widely trusted by browsers, operating systems, and also within Cloudflare.
Because the keys themselves are weak, an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic.
This is a serious security incident with implications across the Internet.
For reference, here is a link to more information about how SSL certificates work and why they are so critical to the operation of the Internet.

articles.title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.
details: Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs , a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain .

Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.

To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.
The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation.
A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible.

articles.title: How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills
articles.excerpt: As Cybersecurity Awareness Month continues, the GitHub Bug Bounty team spotlights @r31n, diving into their research approach, favorite bug classes, and advice for aspiring hackers. The post How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: As Cybersecurity Awareness Month continues, the GitHub Bug Bounty team is excited to spotlight another top-performing security researcher from the GitHub Security Bug Bounty Program: @r31n !

As home to the world's developers, GitHub is dedicated to the security and reliability of the code behind millions of projects, and our Bug Bounty Program remains a cornerstone of that commitment. Collaboration with external researchers is one of the most effective ways to improve security, and every year, the community helps us identify and fix vulnerabilities that make the platform safer for everyone.
AI has lowered the barrier to entry and become a genuine force multiplier.
We use it across our own internal security programs, and we welcome researchers who do the same .
However, what separates great research has not changed: validation, a working proof of concept, and a clear demonstration of real security impact.

articles.title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare has achieved South Korea's ISMS certification following an audit across 80 controls. Learn how we localized user consent flows, adapted social sign-up paths at the edge, and validated our global security program.
details: For ten days, auditors appointed by the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) sat together with us and worked through 80 controls. That is what it took for a company headquartered in the United States, operating a global network serving Korean users, to be certified in South Korea. Cloudflare has now obtained South Korea's Information Security Management System (ISMS) certification under the ISMS-P framework .

For customers in Korea, this is more than a compliance checkbox. It is evidence that Cloudflare's security and privacy program has been examined not only for whether our controls exist, but for how they operate in the context of Korean law, the Korean language, and the particular expectations of Korean regulators.

A user signing up from South Korea sees something different. The Korean experience is triggered by the country selected at sign-up and by IP geolocation from within South Korea, and it breaks the same agreement into four separately labeled items, each marked required or optional, each linking to its full text, with an option to agree to all of them at once:
[필수] 개인정보 수집 및 이용 ([Required] Collection and use of personal information)
[필수] 제한된 범위의 개인정보 해외 이전 ([Required] Transfer of a limited amount of personal information overseas)

articles.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare's web application firewall can now correlate an HTTP request with its response. Full transaction detection helps every customer find successful exploits, data exposure, and risky misconfigurations that request-only inspection can miss.
details: Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules.
Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation.
It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester.

These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix - and attackers new paths to exploit.
The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk.

articles.title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
articles.excerpt: Fast, focused, low-cost decisions for any application.
details: Applications and agents make many small decisions throughout a workflow: how to classify an input, where to route a request, or which action to take next.
Today, we’re making the Decisions API generally available.

Built with GPT‑6 Luna, the Decisions API focuses Luna’s intelligence on questions with bounded answers, helping applications and agents make near real-time decisions from text, images, and structured inputs up to 10x faster than GPT‑6 Luna through the Responses API.
Since public beta, we’ve added a native GPT‑Live integration, prompt caching for reused context, and inference residency in the US and EU.
Developers can also pass native JSON inputs, include images in question instructions, and ask up to 400 questions per request, twice the previous limit.

articles.title: How 3 Java Champions are using GitHub Copilot for increased productivity
articles.excerpt: Three Java Champions share how they use GitHub Copilot to solve problems, accelerate development, and keep humans responsible for the results. The post How 3 Java Champions are using GitHub Copilot for increased productivity appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: AI coding tools can generate code quickly, but speed alone does not solve the hardest software engineering problems. Developers still need to provide context, validate results, protect maintainability, and remain accountable for what ships.

To learn how experienced developers strike that balance, we spoke with three Java Champions, all with over a decade of experience in using Java. They shared concrete examples of using GitHub Copilot in production and open source, along with the practices they use to turn AI-generated output into reliable software.
Vlad Mihalcea , founder of Hypersistence and author of the book High-Performance Java Persistence
Patrick Baumgartner , software crafter at 42talents with 20+ years of Java experience
Frank Delporte , senior technical writer at Azul and maintainer of Foojay.io with 15+ years of Java experience

articles.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform
articles.excerpt: From local businesses to global brands, more advertisers can now reach people as they explore, compare and decide what to buy in ChatGPT.
details: More than 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week to explore ideas, compare options and make decisions.
Ads can help people discover products and services that fit their needs, including options they might not have found otherwise.
Since we launched ads just over eight months ago, over 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns on ChatGPT.
Today, we’re expanding ChatGPT Ads to 26 additional countries, extending availability to 89 countries worldwide.

This launch builds on our recent expansions across[](http://openai.com/index/chatgpt-ads-expands-across-europe/)Europe and[](http://openai.com/index/chatgpt-ads-expands-southeast-asia-taiwan/)Southeast Asia and Taiwan.
